provenance.title: Reference catalogue of major landslide events in the North Eastern Region
provenance.description: A short, deliberately conservative catalogue of major, publicly documented landslide or landslide-generating events. It is NOT a landslide inventory: a survey inventory has hundreds to thousands of individually mapped polygons. This catalogue exists so that the historical-evidence layer has real, checkable content on a fresh checkout, and is merged with (and outweighed by) any imported GSI/institutional inventory.
provenance.accuracy: Each event is tied to a named district rather than a mapped polygon, so `lat`/`lon` are the event area's reference point. Dates follow the published record; where the published record gives a range, the date is the principal reported day. `confidence` is `documented` where a published post-event study exists and `reported` where the event appears in the contemporary record but no detailed study was consulted.
references: Oldham, R.D. (1899) Report on the Great Earthquake of 12th June 1897
GSI records of the 15th August 1950 Assam-Tibet earthquake
Post-event landslide inventories for the 18th September 2011 Sikkim earthquake
CWC / state government and district administration reports for the June 2022 Assam-Meghalaya event
NDMA and Sikkim state reports on the 4th October 2023 South Lhonak GLOF

events.summary: Synchronous landsliding over the whole plateau: rockfalls, debris slides and blocking of the Umiam and other valley floors. The largest single landslide event on record in the region, and the reason the plateau's scarps remain unstable today.
Hundreds of rock avalanches and debris slides across the eastern Himalaya. River courses were dammed and then burst, and hillslopes left unconsolidated were reported to fail in subsequent monsoons.
Foothill slope failure and bank collapse on the Brahmaputra margin, with the aggradation of the river by landslide sediment as a secondary hazard.

events.magnitude_note: Cloudburst rainfall over the Sikkim-Darjeeling Himalaya
events.summary: A multi-day rainstorm in early October 1968 produced widespread slope failure and debris flow in the Teesta and Rangit catchments. The exact principal day is not consistently reported, hence the `reported` grade.
More than three hundred landslides were mapped after the event in the Teesta basin. NH-10 was severed at multiple points and the Lachung and Lachen valleys were cut off.
Co-seismic rockfalls and shallow debris slides on cut slopes around the state capital; the cause of most of the event's casualties through building collapse under slope failure.
A long June rain spell triggered slope failures on the hill road and rail alignments through the Barail range, closing the Guwahati-Silchar route for days.

events.place: Meghalaya plateau scarp (Ri Bhoi, West Khasi Hills)
events.summary: Pre-monsoon cyclonic rainfall on already saturated ground produced slope failures along the Guwahati-Shillong and Shillong-Silchar corridors.

events.magnitude_note: Record June rainfall over the Barail range
events.summary: The most severe road-closure event of the last decade in Assam: landslides cut both the hill road alignment and the Lumding-Badarpur rail line, isolating Dima Hasao for weeks and forcing a long diversion via the Barak valley.

events.magnitude_note: Extreme June rainfall totals on the plateau scarp
events.summary: Sustained monsoon rainfall re-activated multiple scarp failures, blocking the Shillong-Silchar road and flooding the low ground below the escarpment.
The Barak valley's worst flood in living memory combined with slope failures in the adjoining Barail and Mizo foothills, cutting both road and rail access to the valley.

events.place: South Lhonak GLOF, North Sikkim (Chungthang, Mangan, Dikchu)
events.magnitude_note: Glacial lake outburst flood on the South Lhonak lake
events.summary: A glacial lake outburst sent a debris flow down the Teesta, destroying the Chungthang dam and cutting NH-10 at numerous points by both the flow itself and associated slope failures. The clearest recent demonstration that hazard in the region is not rainfall-only.

events.magnitude_note: Early monsoon rainfall on slopes left unstable by the 2023 GLOF
events.summary: Landslides and debris flows during the first major monsoon spell after the GLOF, on slopes whose toe support had been removed the previous October.
